text:
sam: quick heads-up — noticed a 10–15% regression on 95th latency for short seqs after yesterday's runtime changes. traces point to increased host-side prep time (tokenize + parse + stream chunking). attaching quick notes.

jess: ugh, ok. any obvious culprits from the flamegraphs?

sam: flame shows tokenization up from ~1.8ms -> ~4.1ms on p50 of short requests, parsing (header/json) from 0.4ms -> 1.0ms. grpc/http layer also shows a bump (~0.6ms -> 1.2ms) due to extra allocations in streaming path.

perf-bot: CI perf-run: build 2026-03-16 vs baseline — p95 end-to-end +12%. breakdown: tokenizer +1.9ms, parser +0.6ms, stream-chunking +0.5ms, kv-cache memcpy +0.8ms.

kai: interesting that kv-cache memcpy is showing — are we copying KV on every request because of new buffer ownership semantics? that would explain the memcpy hit.

sam: yes, change in last PR made RequestBuffer own the KV slice for safety; we ended up copying into per-request vector on parse.

rohan: can we switch to shared arena or ref-counted span to avoid copy? we should also check our tokenizer instance churn — creating tokenizer per-request will allocate the vocab map repeatedly.

maria: I profiled allocator hot paths. Lots of small allocations in tokenizer + JSON parsing. switching to a slab allocator for small objects cut p50 prep time on my local harness by ~30%.

jess: would that interact badly with the pool safety invariants for private deployments? need to ensure no leak across requests in dedicated host.

maria: slab per-worker thread + periodic reset on worker tick keeps isolation. it's what eng-infra did for rpc buffers.

sam: another low-hanging: streaming chunking currently does a memcpy when assembling frames for grpc-stream; if we pre-chunk and reference slices we can avoid an extra copy at the cost of slightly more complex lifecycle.

kai: also kernel-selection / batching angle: small seqs currently route to kernel K1 which expects packed inputs; our host-side aligner is padding and copying to match K1 layout. if we route small seqs to K2 (supports variable length) we avoid the host-side pack. Need perf matrix for K1 vs K2 for short seqs.

rohan: good call. can we add an experiment flag to route by sequence-length threshold and measure end-to-end? keep kv-cache behavior constant.

sam: yes — I'll flip routing and run the perf harness.

perf-bot: suggestion: nightly job to run microbenchmarks that isolate tokenization and parse times (no GPU) and compare across commits. we don't currently surface those metrics in the console dashboards.

jess: add that and an alert for >10% delta on host-prep p95. also add a churn metric for tokenizer instance creation.

maria: quick patch I tried locally (slab allocator + avoid KV copy by using read-only span + reuse tokenizer per-worker) — results: tokenization p50 down 25%, parse p50 down 40%, end-to-end p95 down 8% on short-seq harness. x86 local numbers attached.

sam: can you open a PR with the slab + span changes behind a feature flag? we'll run it through the staging perf matrix (kernel routing variants + batching heuristics).

maria: will do. PR will include benchmark script:
```
# run microbench for host prep
./tools/bench_host_prep --requests=10000 --seq-len=32 --threads=8 --flag-slab=true --flag-reuse-tokenizer=true
```

kai: one more note: HTTP/gRPC overhead — enable keep-alive for short-lived flows and reuse the HTTP2 connection where possible. some clients were opening new connections per request in the test harness which amplified observed host costs due to TLS handshake.

sam: good catch. I saw a subset of failing traces with TLS handshake time baked in. we've got two vectors: client churn + our extra copies.

rohan: plan of action: 1) maria opens PR w/ slab + span + reuse tokenizer behind flag, 2) sam toggles kernel routing in staging and runs perf matrix, 3) add microbench job and dashboard alerts, 4) enforce client keep-alive in harness and verify gRPC settings.

jess: assign owners and ETA?

sam: maria +1 for PR today. I'll run routing matrix tomorrow morning. kai can you update harness to enforce keep-alive before tomorrow's run? rohan will add the alert rule.

maria: PR incoming in ~2h. posting perf diffs in thread once CI finishes. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: CI-note: when posting diffs include p50/p95 for host-tokenize, host-parse, stream-chunk, kv-copy, and end-to-end. attach flamegraphs if possible.

sam: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the staging runs.
